help.text:
Kaleidoscope local memory runtime

Usage:
  kscope --help
  kscope --version
  kscope model
  kscope public-contract
  kscope licences
  kscope init <ROOT> <RFC3339_CREATED_AT> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope init-profile <NAME> <ROOT> <RFC3339_CREATED_AT> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope profile create <NAME> <ROOT> <WORKSPACE_ID> <PRINCIPAL_ID> <JOURNAL> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope profile import <NAME> <ROOT> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope profile list
  kscope profile show <NAME>
  kscope profile remove <NAME>
  kscope profile launch <NAME>
  kscope vault-preview <ROOT>
  kscope vault-delete <ROOT>
  kscope vault-migrate <ROOT>
  kscope vault-verify <ROOT> [--cross-backend]
  kscope vault-create <REPOSITORY> <RFC3339_CREATED_AT>
  kscope vault-open <REPOSITORY>
  kscope vault-close <REPOSITORY>
  kscope vault-recover <REPOSITORY>
  kscope vault-export-device <REPOSITORY> <NEW_PACKAGE_DIRECTORY>
  kscope vault-import-device <PACKAGE_DIRECTORY> <REPOSITORY>
  kscope vault-encrypted-preview <REPOSITORY>
  kscope vault-encrypted-delete <REPOSITORY>
  kscope mcp <ROOT> <WORKSPACE_ID> <PRINCIPAL_ID> <JOURNAL> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope serve <ROOT> <WORKSPACE_ID> <PRINCIPAL_ID> <JOURNAL> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope context <ROOT> <WORKSPACE_ID> <PRINCIPAL_ID> <JOURNAL> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope call <ROOT> <WORKSPACE_ID> <PRINCIPAL_ID> <JOURNAL> <OPERATION> [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope mcp --profile <NAME>
  kscope serve --profile <NAME>
  kscope context --profile <NAME>
  kscope call --profile <NAME> <OPERATION>
  kscope schema [OPERATION]
  kscope where
  kscope mcp [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope serve [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope context [process-local|durable-local]
  kscope call <OPERATION> [process-local|durable-local]

The four commands that address a vault accept the four ids or none of them.
Naming none resolves them: KSCOPE_ROOT, else `.kaleidoscope/` under the
repository's main checkout, else `.kaleidoscope/` under the working directory --
and then the vault's own workspace record for the workspace, principal and
journal, so naming the root names all four. KSCOPE_WORKSPACE,
KSCOPE_PRINCIPAL and KSCOPE_JOURNAL override that record field by field, and
are how a vault holding more than one workspace is disambiguated.

Arguments always win, and win completely: an invocation naming the four ids
never reads the environment at all. That is what keeps every existing caller
byte-identical.

A resolved root that is not a vault is REFUSED, naming the path and where the
path came from. It is never created -- `kscope init` remains the only way a
vault comes into existence, and it takes its ROOT explicitly, because a wrong
root is not an error, it is a different vault.

A version-1 profile is a non-secret pointer to one existing vault identity. It
stores an absolute root, workspace, principal, journal and durability under the
platform configuration directory's `kaleidoscope/profiles`, or exactly under
KSCOPE_PROFILE_HOME when that override is set. Profile names are portable and
path-safe; profile files are atomic, owner-only on Unix and validated against
the vault each time they are loaded. `profile import` derives the identity from
the selected vault; `profile create` verifies the explicit tuple. Neither one
creates or relocates canonical vault data.

`init-profile` is the native fresh-bootstrap primitive. It initializes the
explicit root, then writes the named profile. If the second step fails, it does
not delete the committed vault; the refusal reports the exact root and a
machine-readable recovery argv for `kscope profile import`. Durable-local is
never silently downgraded and remains refused before initialization effects.

`profile launch` prints a versioned stdio launch descriptor pointing directly
at this absolute engine executable with `mcp --profile NAME`. The descriptor
names only `search` and `remember` and contains no vault coordinates or secret.
Explicit four-coordinate invocations remain the compatibility authority and do
not read KSCOPE_PROFILE_HOME.

The where command prints the address these rules resolve to, as JSON, and
resolves nothing else. Every command that resolved rather than was told also
prints the same on stderr, unprompted, because a caller relying on a default
cannot check a root it did not type. stdout stays exactly what it was.

The licences command prints the attribution for third-party material this
executable redistributes inside itself. The embedded embedding table is
MinishLab's, under MIT, and MIT requires its notice to accompany every copy --
which a one-file release cannot do with a NOTICE beside the binary. `licenses`
is accepted as a spelling. The output states what it does not yet cover.

The model command prints one JSON object naming the semantic embedding model
this executable carries, its table dtype, and the SHA-256 of its two files, or
reports that this build has none. A release must report one: the release
installer refuses a package whose executable does not.

The public-contract command prints a small source-free JSON seed for release
contract generation. It opens no vault and loads no model.

The vault-recover command reads a JSON object containing recovery_key from
stdin. The two delete commands require their preview command's
confirmation_token in a JSON object on stdin. Encrypted repository vaults are
a frozen macOS-preview feature.

The optional serve command uses a Unix-domain socket and is unavailable on
non-Unix platforms. The stdio mcp command and process-scoped call command do
not depend on it.

The vault-migrate command builds the storage engine's index over a vault
written by the older fs-v0 engine. It creates, moves, copies and deletes no
content file, re-runs safely, works on a vault whose journal has rotated, and
is undone by deleting one file -- until the first write through the engine.
Run vault-verify after it and before writing. Neither command reads the
journal, so both work on a vault this executable cannot otherwise open.

The context command reads one search JSON request from stdin and prints only
the concise model-visible memory text. call search returns the bounded public
result, including final rank and fused score on selected hits; private
policy/ranker feature vectors, the signed decision payload and engine
diagnostics are omitted. The documented public workflow has no supported
outcome-attribution path until a future authenticated manager/controller
interface exchanges a keyed opaque handle. This is an API contract, not an
authentication claim about the local vault.

The call command reads one JSON request from stdin. OPERATION is one of:

  AGENT     search | remember
  OPERATOR  feedback | memory_lifecycle | memory_import | address_maintenance
            maintenance | ontology | doctor

Only the two agent verbs are published as MCP tools. search merges what were
recall, compile and read_memory: a query ranks and a memory_id addresses. A
ranked search always writes the exposure row and bounds the served set --
ledger: false was a second door and is refused, so a measurement that must not
write to a vault has to clone it first. Its four knobs are top_k,
candidate_pool, bfs_depth and max_facts, each with a published default and
ceiling.

The schema command prints one OPERATION's full descriptive parameters and
closed values. MCP derives a versioned compact, omission-first inputSchema from
the same operation semantics. The two preserve the same non-null machine
constraints but are intentionally not byte-identical: the native decoder
accepts legacy explicit null while MCP omits absent optionals. Pass no OPERATION
to list them.

operation_schemas.name: remember
operation_schemas.text:
remember

Write memory: create, update, or delete one, or create several in order.

AGENT VERB — published as an MCP tool.

  mode (required)
    What this write does.
    closed — one of:
      create  write a new memory
      update  replace an existing memory's content and facts
      delete  logically delete one memory
  memory_id (optional)
    Required for update/delete; for create it is derived from the retry identity.
  content_md (optional)
    Markdown beginning with `# ` for create/update; omitted for delete and for a batch, which carries its markdown per item.
  semantic_delta (optional)
    The validated semantic structure committed with create/update, with at least one fact; omit for delete.
  expected_version_id (optional)
    The active version update/delete is allowed to replace. Required for update/delete and omitted for create.
  items (optional)
    Several creates in one call, applied in order, instead of content_md/semantic_delta. Every item declares its own title and facts -- nothing is shared or inherited between them. Use it when you have already extracted several memories in one reasoning step; a batch does not invent IDs or a hidden supersession edge between items. An item this call cannot accept is refused on its own and the others are still written: the response reports it at its index with status `refused` and the reason, so repair that item and resend only it. That isolation is per-item VALIDATION. A field this schema does not name fails deserialization instead, which happens before any item is written and costs the whole call, so resend all of it.
      content_md
      semantic_delta
        admission — Optional write-value evidence: four finite 0..1 signals; explicit_user_intent defaults false.
          confidence
          durability
          explicit_user_intent
          recurrence
          utility
        context — The verbatim source text this memory was extracted from. Stored so a reader can check the extraction against what was said; it is never parsed.
        contradicts
        corrections — Corrections to what the vault already holds. Nothing gates a correction — a system where fixing a memory is harder than writing one accumulates errors.
          handle — The handle the correction is about.
          says — What is being corrected.
        entities — Every entity your facts name. Declare all of them or none: a half-declared memory resolves half its mentions on a worse probe. A DATE IS NEVER AN ENTITY — times go in `occurred_at`, a fact's `from`/`until`, or an `about` key.
          is — A one-line gloss. REQUIRED, and it is not documentation — it is what the matcher probes with. `opus 5` alone matches on four characters; `opus 5 | model | Anthropic language model` is what actually finds the node you meant.
          kind — Known here: artifact, capability, concept, doc, event, metric, model, org, person, place, practice, tool. New values are accepted. A novel kind only shifts kind_compat's score, and it is useful immediately when it arrives with its is_a edge. Minting one is 3-zone threshold.
          n — The surface your facts refer to this entity by, spelled as they spell it.
        evidence — Inspectable local evidence references; never hidden model reasoning.
          digest — Optional content digest of the referenced evidence.
          kind — Evidence class, such as `file`, `test`, or `user_statement`.
          reference — Locator, such as a path, URL, or identifier.
        facts
          about — Qualifiers on this fact. Each key's declared class decides how its value is read: a referential value is resolved against the graph exactly as a mention is, an ordinal value is checked against the closed scale, a literal value is validated and not resolved.
            <any key> — A string for a referential or ordinal key, a number for a quantity, or a `{t, grain}` object for a time.
            <key> — Known here: amount, certainty, degree, for, instrument, priority, scope, source, unit, when. New values are accepted. A novel key only shifts matching — but without a declared class KScope cannot tell whether to resolve its value or validate it. Minting one is 3-zone threshold, and a declared class — referential, ordinal or literal.
          basis — background = the model knows it; the text does not say it; implied = the text presupposes or entails it; stated = the text says it. Closed: it feeds the base term of the confidence formula, base(basis) × corroboration ÷ contention × decay (design §4.2). [one of: background, implied, stated]
          because — The `f` ids of the facts in THIS memory that justify this one. Ids, never positions.
          confidence
          evidence
          f — This fact's id within this memory, so `because` has something to reference. Number every fact if any fact uses `because`.
          from — When this fact starts being true. Absent inherits the memory's `occurred_at`.
            grain — Which period `t` names. Send the grain the memory actually supported: `March` is `{"t": "2026-03", "grain": "month"}` and never `2026-03-01`. [one of: year, month, day, hour, instant]
            t — The value at the grain below: `2026`, `2026-03`, `2026-03-15`, `2026-03-15T09`, or an RFC 3339 timestamp. The grain is read FIRST and selects the form this is decoded at; nothing infers the form from the value.
          mode — fact = a statement about the world; preference = what the subject would choose, other things equal; decision = a choice that was made and stands until something supersedes it; procedure = a reusable way of doing something; outcome = what happened when something was tried, attributable to it; event = something that occurred at a time. Closed: it feeds the decay rate, the default retrievability, and supersession eligibility. [one of: fact, preference, decision, procedure, outcome, event]
          object
          predicate — Known here: authored, avoids, blocked_by, caused, costs, decided, depends_on, instance_of, made_by, measured_at, owned_by, part_of, powers, prefers, stopped_using, strong_at, switched_to, uses, weak_at, worked_on. Refused, emitted by the fold: contradicts, justified_by, not_same_as, possibly_same_as, same_as, supersedes. New values are accepted. A novel verb only shifts the definition probe's score — but two predicates for one relation split every fact of it, so reuse before you propose. Minting one is 3-zone threshold, and a semantics proposal — means, from, to, many, over_time.
          subject
          until — When it stops. Absent stays absent — it never inherits, because the memory default is a start and inheriting it as an end would close every open interval in the vault.
            grain — Which period `t` names. Send the grain the memory actually supported: `March` is `{"t": "2026-03", "grain": "month"}` and never `2026-03-01`. [one of: year, month, day, hour, instant]
            t — The value at the grain below: `2026`, `2026-03`, `2026-03-15`, `2026-03-15T09`, or an RFC 3339 timestamp. The grain is read FIRST and selects the form this is decoded at; nothing infers the form from the value.
        memory_type — Workspace ontology type. Reuse an accepted name rather than coining a near-synonym: types are append-only, so `user_preference` and `preference` would both persist forever.
        occurred_at — When this memory's facts are about. YOU resolve the time — `last Tuesday` becomes an absolute value with a grain, or this stays null. Kaleidoscope parses no date out of prose. A fact with no `from` of its own inherits this, and the claim records that it inherited.
          grain — Which period `t` names. Send the grain the memory actually supported: `March` is `{"t": "2026-03", "grain": "month"}` and never `2026-03-01`. [one of: year, month, day, hour, instant]
          t — The value at the grain below: `2026`, `2026-03`, `2026-03-15`, `2026-03-15T09`, or an RFC 3339 timestamp. The grain is read FIRST and selects the form this is decoded at; nothing infers the form from the value.
        propose — Relations you believe you are inventing. Sending none is itself a claim — that the verbs you used already exist. A proposal is active immediately; it is what lets a relation supersede rather than accumulate.
          from — The declared domain kinds.
          inverse — Optional, and yours alone to supply: nothing computes an inverse from a definition, and a wrong one makes every claim readable backwards under a verb the vault never agreed to.
          many — Whether one subject may hold several objects at once. It puts the object on the slot key, so it decides what may collide.
          means — The definition. It dominates the matching probe — a proposal without one is a name, and names are low signal.
          over_time — Whether supersession applies to this relation at all. [one of: event, state, immutable]
          rel — Known here: authored, avoids, blocked_by, caused, costs, decided, depends_on, instance_of, made_by, measured_at, owned_by, part_of, powers, prefers, stopped_using, strong_at, switched_to, uses, weak_at, worked_on. Refused, emitted by the fold: contradicts, justified_by, not_same_as, possibly_same_as, same_as, supersedes. New values are accepted. A novel verb only shifts the definition probe's score — but two predicates for one relation split every fact of it, so reuse before you propose. Minting one is 3-zone threshold, and a semantics proposal — means, from, to, many, over_time.
          to — The declared range kinds.
        scope — Where this memory applies. An omitted axis matches every request; a set axis matches only that exact value.
          artifact
          branch
          project
        temporal — Validity interval. A memory whose `valid_until` has passed is not served.
          valid_from
          valid_until
        title — The memory's title, in your words. It is not scraped out of `content_md` (ADR 0053): you already know the title you wrote, and recovering it by parsing the rendered form makes the display format load-bearing and mis-titles any memory whose body does not open with an H1.

operation_schemas.name: search
operation_schemas.text:
search

Read memory in exactly one mode. A `query` ranks, bounds the served context, and writes an exposure row. A `memory_id` returns one exact current record, runs no ranking or filtering, and accepts none of the ranked controls.

AGENT VERB — published as an MCP tool.

  query (optional)
    Ranked selection: what to search for. Supply exactly one of query and memory_id.
  memory_id (optional)
    Addressed selection: the `mem_...` identity to return. It ranks, filters, and compiles no served set, so ranked-only controls below do not apply and supplying one alongside it is refused rather than ignored.
  top_k (optional)
    Ranked query only. Maximum memories to serve, in ranked order. It changes the amount of context the caller receives, so evaluations compare runs only at the same value. Omission uses the published default; values above the published ceiling are refused.
  candidate_pool (optional)
    Ranked query only. How many candidates each enabled retrieval channel may propose before the final served-set cut. It is independent of top_k. Omission uses the published default; values above the published ceiling are refused.
  bfs_depth (optional)
    Ranked query only. Maximum relationship hops considered while expanding connected memory context. max_facts remains the independent fact budget. Omission uses the published default; values above the published ceiling are refused.
  max_facts (optional)
    Ranked query only. Maximum connected facts that may be added to served memory context. Omission uses the published default; values above the published ceiling are refused.
  ledger (optional)
    Ranked query only. Write an exposure-ledger row and bound the served set to maximum_context_bytes. It defaults to true and FALSE IS REFUSED, not silently upgraded: a caller that asked for a read-only search and quietly got a write would put a row into a store it believed it was only reading. So a ranked search is always a write, and a measurement that must not write has to clone the vault. Omit this field for memory_id, which writes no exposure row.
    closed — one of:
      true  write the required exposure row and apply the context bound
  maximum_context_bytes (optional)
    Ranked query only. The byte budget the served set is bounded to. Omission uses the published default.
  as_of (optional)
    Ranked query only. RFC3339 instant validity is evaluated at. Omitted means now, not `ignore validity`.
  scope (optional)
    Ranked query only. Restrict the served set to one project/branch/artifact. An omitted axis matches every memory.
  channels (optional)
    Ranked query only. Restrict which retrieval channels may contribute candidates. Omit for normal serving, which runs every channel; naming a subset is how a channel's contribution is measured.

schema_index.text:
kscope schema <OPERATION>

Two agent verbs, published as MCP tools:
  search
  remember

Operator commands, in no agent tool list:
  feedback
  memory_lifecycle
  memory_import
  address_maintenance
  maintenance
  ontology
  doctor

input_schema.description: H1; 1-32 facts; update/delete need expected_version_id; Batch: create-only/exclusive; rel/kind are open; active immediately; n/kind/is matcher gloss; entities/evidence32 propose8 corrections/contradicts16 f/because>=0 confidence/admission 0..1.

tools.description: query ranks+writes; memory_id reads; top_k protocol-defining~5.
tools.name: search
